panels.title: Primacy bias: share of 'complex' by option order
panels.description: Jev's route choice split by which option was listed first. Live traffic uses one fixed order today (standard first), so only one bar appears until orders vary. If the two bars differ on the same messages, that is primacy bias.

targets.rawSql: SELECT option_order[1] || '-first' AS "order", round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE choice = 'complex') / count(*), 1) AS pct_complex FROM jev_assessments WHERE $__timeFilter(finished_at) AND question = 'route' AND status = 'ok' AND option_order IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

targets.rawSql: SELECT intent_first AS "first (message only)", intent_second AS "second (message + reply)", count(*) AS requests FROM jev_reply_checks WHERE $__timeFilter(finished_at) AND intent_agrees = false GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 20

options.content:
The **first** Jev call runs before the model and sees only the customer's message. The **second** call is optional and off by default. It runs after the reply is built, sees the message and the reply, answers the route and intent questions again, and says whether the reply fits. It costs one extra Jev call per checked request and never delays the customer.

*Qwen vs Jev intent agreement* (Reply quality) is a different measure: the model's own label against the first call. The standard-first vs complex-first comparison needs the order-swap run (PRs #89, #90).
